title: Neptune Has Had Only One Birthday Since We Found It

scenes.text: Neptune has had just one birthday since humans discovered it.
Astronomers first spotted Neptune in eighteen forty-six. It's so far out that one lap around the Sun takes about a hundred and sixty-five Earth years.
So it only finished its first orbit since discovery in July twenty eleven. Everyone alive at the discovery was long gone.
And here's the twist. Nobody saw Neptune first. A mathematician found it with a pencil, by working out what was tugging on Uranus.
It takes so long because Neptune sits thirty times farther from the Sun than we do.
Its second birthday is due around twenty one seventy-six. Who do you think will be around to celebrate?

description:
Neptune has completed only one orbit of the Sun since humans discovered it.
It was found in 1846, but a Neptune year lasts about 165 Earth years, so its first full lap since discovery ended in July 2011. The planet was located by mathematics first: astronomers calculated where an unseen planet must be from its pull on Uranus, then pointed a telescope and found it.
It orbits so slowly because it is about 4.5 billion km from the Sun, 30 times farther than Earth.
Who will be around for its next birthday in 2176?
